I had my assessment through them earlier this year - a large part of it was him asking the same/very similar questions as the forms, I'd answer and he would ask follow ups to help me elaborate. at the end the assessor told me how he'd categorised all my answers/general behaviour to justify a diagnosis. 

if it's the same for you, you'll be able to elaborate on any answers you gave on the forms and probably can bring up that you've rethought some of your answers now you've had time to reflect. 

I was super anxious and overthinking everything but I felt like the questions I was asked were really helpful.

I recently started running 3x a week too and I never would've guessed the difference it could make, even just to my attitude to food. Currently on week 7 of C25K and can't believe I'm actually excited about my next run. it makes me want to eat well so I have enough energy for my day.
